A separate part of the trip is devoted to the Festival of the Virgin of Candelaria in Puno. In early February, processions, music, a costumed parade and the traditional devil dance fill the city.

## Trip highlights

Lima introduces you to Peru's colonial architecture and ancient cultures. In Cusco and the Sacred Valley, the programme takes you to Inca monuments, including Sacsayhuamán, Qorikancha, Tambomachay, Puka Pukara, Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero and Moray.

Machu Picchu is one of the central stops on the route. From there, the journey continues across the Peruvian Altiplano to Puno and Lake Titicaca.

Between cities, you will encounter high mountain passes, markets, small settlements, archaeological sites and views of the Andes. This is a long itinerary, with sightseeing days alternating with travel days, and each region of Peru noticeably different from the last.

In Puno, you will experience the Festival of the Virgin of Candelaria. The main costumed parade takes place on 2 February, accompanied by music, processions and traditional dances.

The route then continues to Colca Canyon, Arequipa and the Nazca Desert. A flight in a small aircraft over the Nazca Lines is included in the programme, followed on the Paracas coast by a boat tour to the Ballestas Islands.
